result.title: How Far Can You Steer? Behavior-Capability Frontiers in Contrastive Activation Addition
result.summary: Activation steering can modify language-model behavior without parameter updates, but behavioral efficacy alone does not determine whether an intervention is usable. Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) steers targeted behaviors using activation directions derived from contrasting examples, potentially degrading unrelated model capabilities in the process. We therefore study CAA through a behavior-capability frontier, selecting interventions that maximize behavioral gain subject to an explicit bound on capability degradation. We evaluate this framework across four instruction-tuned models, seven behaviors, and capability-loss budgets of 1%, 3%, and 5% (absolute percentage points). Validation-selected behavioral effects generalize strongly to held-out data ($ρ= 0.945$), while joint behavior-capability survival among nonzero operating points rises from 37.5% at the 1% budget to 72.7% at 3%, with limited additional improvement at 5%. Control experiments indicate that these effects depend on learned behavior directions rather than generic activation perturbations. Representational geometry is significantly but only modestly predictive of causal cross-behavior transfer. Finally, secondary capability, out-of-distribution, and open-ended evaluations show that interventions satisfying protected benchmarks can still degrade untested capabilities or transfer unevenly to free-form generation. These results characterize activation steering as a constrained intervention whose usable range depends on model, behavior, direction, layer, and evaluation budget, rather than a universal control knob.

AI.brief_summary: 论文围绕对比激活引导（CAA）研究行为收益与能力损伤的权衡，提出“行为—能力前沿”框架，在四个指令微调模型、七种行为和 1%/3%/5% 能力损失预算下筛选干预，并检验行为效应泛化、表示几何对跨行为迁移的预测力以及未测能力的副作用。
AI.relevance_reason: 把内部激活方向的施加视为有明确代价预算的约束型干预，并用表示几何预测因果迁移，这可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态干预的收益—成本刻画与表示相似度解读，但尚未涉及视觉或多模态推理。
